title: tar-stream + shard mismatch debugging notes
content:
Context:
- Hit intermittent model loads failing in private deployment when pulling model tarball from GCS signed URLs. Failure window tight: 2–10% of requests. Appears after looping many cold-starts (autoscale spike).
- Symptoms: process dies during unpack, downstream loader reports missing tensors or checksum mismatch. No consistent shard id reported, sometimes last shard.

Hypothesis list (high priority first):
1) Partial/streaming download truncated due to signed URL expiry or connection cut while piping into tar (curl|gsutil streaming).
2) Tarball contains alternate file ordering vs manifest; loader expects shard01..shardNN contiguously but tar contains interleaved metadata; streaming pipe hits EOF mid-entry.
3) Client-side/mid-transfer gz chunk corrupted (network blip) -> tar reports 'Unexpected EOF' but loader surfaces as missing tensor keys.
4) Format mismatch: some bundles are safetensors, others are torch .pt inside same tar; loader path picks wrong deserializer and silently yields empty tensors.
5) mmap / OOM when mapping large shard file after extraction -> partial readbacks interpreted as corruption.

Commands & captures I ran (local repro attempts):
- quick list without downloading whole tar (to validate manifest ordering):
  curl -sS --fail "${GCS_SIGNED_URL}" | tar -tvf - | head -n 80 > /tmp/tar-head.txt
  # outcome: shows manifest.json at start, then shards: shard-00001.safetensors .. shard-00024.safetensors, then README.txt. ordering looked fine for the sample tar we pulled.

- try streaming extract with retry wrapper (to reproduce):
  for i in 1 2 3; do \n    curl -sf --retry 5 --retry-delay 2 "${GCS_SIGNED_URL}" | pv -s ${TARBALL_SIZE} | tar xzf - -C /tmp/model-test && echo ok && break || sleep 1; \n  done
  # fail case: tar: Unexpected EOF in archive
  # strace of failing tar shows read() returned 0 while still inside a regular file entry.

- checksum tests on downloaded tar vs GCS metadata:
  gsutil ls -L gs://models-prod/foo/model-2024-11-13.tar.gz > /tmp/gsmeta.txt
  gsutil cp gs://models-prod/foo/model-2024-11-13.tar.gz /tmp/model.tar.gz && sha256sum /tmp/model.tar.gz
  # cp succeeded and checksum matched server-side recorded sha256 when using gsutil cp (non-stream).
  # implication: streaming via curl can truncate while gsutil cp (retry-aware) completes.

- ranged downloads to isolate last N MB (to check EOF patterns):
  # fetch tail chunk to see last tar header bytes
  curl -sS -H "Range: bytes=$((TARBALL_SIZE-65536))-$TARBALL_SIZE" "${GCS_SIGNED_URL}" -o /tmp/tail.dat
  tar -tf /tmp/tail.dat || hexdump -C /tmp/tail.dat | head
  # In a failing run, tail chunk ends mid-file header (no 0x0000 end-of-archive blocks).

- verifying in-memory loader behaviour with artificially truncated safetensors file:
  python - <<PY
import safetensors, io, sys
from safetensors.numpy import load_file
b = open('shard-00024.safetensors','rb').read()
for cut in (len(b)-1_000_000, len(b)-100_000, len(b)-10):
    try:
        load_file(io.BytesIO(b[:cut]))
    except Exception as e:
        print('cut', cut, '->', type(e).__name__, str(e)[:200])
PY
  # Outcome: safetensors loader raises ValueError: "unexpected EOF while reading header" for larger cuts; for tiny cuts raises JSONDecodeError.

Observed error snippets from live service logs (redacted):
- "tar: Unexpected EOF in archive"
- "model-loader: shard missing keys: ['transformer.h.23.attn.k_proj.weight']"
- "safetensors.error: header checksum mismatch"
- "OSError: [Errno 12] Cannot allocate memory" (during mapping of shard-00012)
- "HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden" (from gs signed URL renew attempt)

Important correlates:
- Fail rate spikes when autoscaler fires and multiple nodes concurrently stream the same tar via signed URL.
- gsutil cp (which writes full object then tar -xzf) rarely fails -> suggests streaming via pipe increases exposure to transient network truncation.
- Some failures coincide with signed URL TTL exactly 60s; in logs the download duration ~66s for large models.

Quick mitigation attempted (prod-sandbox):
- changed pull path to use gsutil cp to local disk then tar extract (slower, but more robust). Result: fail rate dropped to near-zero.
- added retry loop with exponential backoff around curl | tar pipe; small improvement but still some tail failures.
- for Dedicated nodes with constrained disk, using tempfs for gsutil cp caused OOM occasionally -> increased swap and bumped node memory.

Open follow-ups / next steps:
- Check signed URL generation TTLs in private control plane (SDK code path). Confirm TTL > largest expected download window + retry budget (suggest 300s for multi-node warmup). Ticketing JIRA-MLINF-879.
- Add server-side pre-signed object HEAD checks before spawning tar extraction to fail fast if object not accessible. (simple HEAD before stream).
- Add optional two-step path in loader: attempt streaming extract; if tar Unexpected EOF or header mismatch -> fall back to atomic copy (gsutil cp or boto3 streaming to disk) then extract. Keep this behind feature flag.
- Instrument more metrics: per-download duration, bytes-read-vs-size, tar EOF flag, signed-url-expires-in header capture.
- Revisit mmap usage: detect OOM mapping and fall back to buffered load to avoid silent partial reads. Catch OSError and surface as explicit 'mmap-failed' error.

Notes on format mixing (safetensors vs torch):
- We saw a single tar that (when extracted fully) contained both .safetensors and .pt; loader should inspect file extension and use appropriate deserializer. Was previously using a heuristic based on manifest entry 'format': ... but manifest was missing in an older bundle. Add manifest validation on upload.

Repro recipe to run locally (quick):
- export GCS_SIGNED_URL from logs (or use sample tar)
- TARBALL_SIZE=$(curl -I -sS "${GCS_SIGNED_URL}" | awk '/Content-Length/{print $2}' | tr -d '')
- run the loop in Commands above to try replicate 'Unexpected EOF'
- use tcpdump on the interface during repro to look for RST or connection reset patterns.

Decision log (temporary):
- Roll forward change: set default signed-url TTL to 5 minutes for model downloads and add HEAD check in private agent. Patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-loader/pull/412

Random breadcrumbs / TODOs (small tasks):
- trace which release introduced streaming-by-pipe behavior (git blame on agent pull path).
- add unit tests to loader that simulate truncated tar stream (feed a socketpair with half the bytes).
- confer with infra networking team about intermittent resets observed in tcpdump (ticket INFRA-NET-204).

If stuck: ping Zara (zara.kim) for reproducer that captured failing tar tail. Ethan has an annotated hexdump that shows tar header truncation pattern.

-- Rowan
